title: M/s Suyash Craft And Papers Ltd. v. Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Tarun Agarwala and Ajay Bhanot, JJ.
disposition: Writ dismissed for want of prosecution.
headnote: Existing consumer alleged tapping of its feeder without Supply Code paragraph 3.4 consent. The Court recorded that paragraph 3.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permits a connection through an original consumer to another consumer only if, among other requirements, the prospective consumer has the original consumer's consent, and accepted the licensee's statement that it would not tap any further consumer to that feeder till further orders. After years of adjournments, the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution when none appeared for the petitioner.
facts: M/s Suyash Craft And Papers Ltd. challenged PVVNL over tapping another consumer onto the feeder serving its connection. On 24 February 2011 the Court noted that paragraph 3.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 allows a connection through an original consumer only with that consumer's consent, which the petitioner said was absent. On 1 March 2011 the licensee stated it would not tap any further consumer to that feeder till further orders. After years of adjournments for a counter-affidavit, none appeared for the petitioner and the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution on 3 October 2017.

holding_units.holding: Paragraph 3.4 of the Supply Code permits a connection through an original consumer to another consumer if, among other requirements, the prospective consumer takes the original consumer's consent. The writ alleging tapping without such consent was later dismissed for want of prosecution, without a merits decision on the tapping dispute.

not_decided.point: Whether tapping another consumer onto the petitioner's feeder without the original consumer's consent violated paragraph 3.4 of the Supply Code
not_decided.note: Petition dismissed for want of prosecution after the licensee's interim statement not to tap further consumers to that feeder.
